checks.detail: Psi sums log p over prime powers p^k<=x with k>=1. It is distinguished from pi, the unweighted prime count. Natural logarithms and actual target-zero zeta zeros are specified.

The supporting exact formula has the correct main term, negative zero sum, negative log(2*pi), and negative half-log correction. It is restricted to real noninteger x>1. The sum uses symmetric height cutoffs and multiplicities rather than arbitrary rearrangement. The half-weight psi_0 convention at a prime-power jump is correct. The short card labels its compressed formula schematic.

For real x>1, x^(beta+i*gamma)=x^beta exp(i*gamma*log x). Conjugate zero contributions combine to real oscillations. RH fixes beta=1/2 for every nontrivial zero, but a moving nonzero-target a-point must not be substituted for such a zero.

The sqrt(x)*log(x)^2 bound is explicitly conditional on RH and asymptotic. The note defines its Big-O meaning, does not assume RH, does not supply an unsupported numerical constant, and explicitly rejects treating this bound for psi-x as an arbitrary finite-sum truncation bound.

The grouping of psi into theta at fractional powers is correct. The stated theta-to-pi integral identity follows by the displayed finite-sum argument, including x=2. The minimum-integer definition of p_n is exact. The text correctly requires counting bounds to isolate a jump before claiming an exact nth prime.

Finite-zero reconstruction, a complete certified zero table, explicit omitted-tail and evaluation bounds, and comparison with a sieve are all future obligations. The chosen half-integer grid avoids jump conventions. No implementation, certificate, improved algorithm, or new RH result is claimed. The conditional RH estimate is not silently used to discharge those obligations.
